title: Protocol-oriented programming: composition instead of inheritance

videos.script: A mock exam is timed, and it is graded. In a tree of classes, it can only have one parent. {{tree}} You will build that tree, and watch a week lose sixty minutes without a single error. {{compose}} Then the same planner, rebuilt from small protocols. One for each thing a type can do. A mock exam lists all of them, and the compiler checks each one. {{mixins}} Then behaviour. Protocol extensions attach it to a capability, so every type that has the capability gets it. {{seam}} Then a protocol used as a seam. A reminder that asks a clock for the time, and a fake clock that is always Monday. {{classes}} And where a class is still the right tool. Shared things, things with a lifetime, and frameworks that hand you a base class.
